scenario: 要在平台规模上分类 文本/图像/视频/音频 内容,同时平衡延迟、精度、成本。
scenario_en: You must classify text/image/video/audio content at platform scale while balancing latency, accuracy, and cost.
q: 内容审核模型架构的三大支柱是什么,数据怎么流？
q_en: What are the three pillars of the moderation model architecture, and how does data flow?
why: 三段流水线:per-modality 编码器 → fusion 融合层 → tiered ensemble 分层集成。每层都输出校准置信度,供分层路由和主动学习使用。
why_en: A three-stage pipeline: per-modality encoders (each modality to a fixed-dim embedding) → a fusion layer that merges the four → a tiered ensemble (fast triage + slow high-accuracy), all emitting calibrated confidence.
diagram:
flowchart LR T["文本编码器"] --> F["fusion 融合层"] I["图像编码器"] --> F V["视频编码器"] --> F A["音频编码器"] --> F F --> E["分层集成
快速 triage + 慢速深判"] E --> O["校准置信度 + 决策"]
options: 单一多分类模型直接吃四路原始模态 → 一步输出全部类别,不设 fusion 也不分层,靠堆参数硬啃差异
先过 CDN 边缘缓存分发,再写入数据库落库,最后跑关键词规则匹配,命中即下架,全程不经过模型
per-modality 编码器 → fusion → 分层集成,全程输出校准置信度
先把全量内容送人工审完,再用这些标签训一个大模型直接上线服务,不设 fusion 层也不分层
options_en: A single multi-class model eats all four raw modalities in one step, skips fusion and tiering entirely, and just piles on parameters to cover the differences.
CDN edge caching first, then write to a database, then keyword rule matching that takes content down on a hit — never passes through a model at all.
Per-modality encoders → fusion → a tiered ensemble, emitting calibrated confidence throughout.
Have humans review everything first, then train one big model on those labels and ship it, with no fusion layer and no tiers.
optionExplanations: 单模型吃不下四种异构模态的类别细微差别,是被明确否定的 monolithic 做法。
CDN/数据库/规则是周边工程,不是审核分类的模型架构。
对;编码→融合→分层三段正是本课骨架,置信度贯穿始终驱动路由与主动学习。
全量人工审在规模上不可行,也不是架构本身,是数据侧的极端做法。
optionExplanations_en: One model can't handle the category nuances across four heterogeneous modalities — the explicitly rejected monolithic approach.
CDN/database/rules are peripheral engineering, not the moderation classification architecture.
Correct — encode → fuse → tier is the lesson's backbone, with confidence throughout driving routing and active learning.
Reviewing everything by hand is infeasible at scale and isn't the architecture itself — an extreme data-side move.

termDefinitions.term: per-modality encoder / 单模态编码器
termDefinitions.meaning: 把某一模态原始输入映射成定长嵌入向量的模型,四个模态各一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A per-modality encoder maps one modality's raw input to a fixed-length embedding, one per modality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把四路模态嵌入合并成一个联合表示、供分类头判定的层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The fusion layer merges the four modality embeddings into one joint representation for the classification heads.

scenario: 有人主张:干脆训练一个大一统模型,把四模态原始数据全喂进去、直接输出所有违规类别。
scenario_en: Someone proposes one monolithic model that ingests all four raw modalities and outputs every violation category directly.
q: 为什么单一大一统模型在内容审核里会失败？
q_en: Why does a single monolithic model fail for content moderation?
why: 不同类别的判据天差地别——meme 里的仇恨言论靠文本语义,视频里的暴力升级靠时序,裸露靠图像。单模型没法同时对每种模态和类别都专精,类别细微差别被平均掉。所以要拆成专门的 per-modality 编码器 + 类别专属分类头。
why_en: Category nuances differ wildly — hate in memes leans on text semantics, video violence on temporal dynamics, nudity on image — so one model can't specialize per modality/category and averages the nuances away.
options: 各类别判据差异极大(仇恨靠文本、暴力靠时序),单模型无法逐一专精
单模型永远达不到 sub-50ms,纯粹是延迟问题,精度上其实没有任何损失
单模型只是参数不够多,无限堆参数和数据就能一统四个模态的判据
单模型只在音频模态上失败,文本、图像、视频它其实都够用
options_en: Category criteria differ hugely — hate leans on text, violence on temporal signal — so one model cannot specialize for each.
A monolith can never hit sub-50ms; it is purely a latency problem with no accuracy loss at all.
The monolith just has too few parameters; unlimited parameters and data would unify all four modalities.
The monolith only fails on audio; it is perfectly fine for text, image, and video.
optionExplanations: 对;每种模态/类别需要不同的专门归纳偏置,单模型把差异摊平,专精组件才抓得住细微差别。
问题主要在精度与类别专精,不只是延迟;把它归为纯延迟问题是误判。
加参数不解决'不同模态需要不同结构'的问题,时序模型和图像模型的归纳偏置本就不同。
单模型在四模态上都难专精,不是只在音频上失败,以偏概全。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — each modality/category needs a different inductive bias, and a monolith flattens the differences while specialized components catch the nuance.
The issue is mainly accuracy and specialization, not just latency; framing it as pure latency is wrong.
Adding parameters doesn't fix 'different modalities need different structures'; temporal and image models have different inductive biases.
A monolith struggles to specialize across all four modalities, not only audio — an overgeneralization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用单一模型吃全部模态、输出全部类别的做法,内容审核里因类别差异大而失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A monolithic model uses one model for all modalities and categories, which fails in moderation due to wide category differences.

scenario: 架构不只要输出'违规/安全',还要输出一个可信的置信度分数。
scenario_en: The architecture must output not just violating/safe but a trustworthy confidence score.
q: 为什么这套审核架构必须输出良好校准的置信度？
q_en: Why must this moderation architecture output well-calibrated confidence?
why: 置信度是两件事的燃料:分层路由(高置信自动、不确定升级)和主动学习飞轮(挑最不确定的送人工)。校准差 → 说的 0.5 不是真 0.5 → 两个机制都跟着跑偏,把错的内容自动处置或送错人。
why_en: Confidence fuels two things: tier routing (auto vs escalate) and the active-learning flywheel (pick the most uncertain for humans), and poor calibration derails both.
options: 只是为了在运营报表里显示一个好看的百分比,没有实际用途
为了让模型训练更快收敛、少跑几个 epoch,与线上路由决策无关
为了替代精度指标,有了置信度就不用再算 precision/recall
置信度驱动分层路由和主动学习选样,校准差会让两者一起跑偏
options_en: Just to show a nice-looking percentage on an ops dashboard, with no real use.
To make training converge faster with fewer epochs, unrelated to online routing decisions.
To replace accuracy metrics — with confidence you no longer need to compute precision/recall.
Confidence drives tier routing and active-learning sample selection, so bad calibration derails both at once.
optionExplanations: 置信度是在线路由与主动学习的核心信号,不是装饰性报表数字。
校准关乎线上决策可信度,不是训练收敛速度。
置信度不能替代 precision/recall,它衡量的是不确定性,不是分类正确率。
对;路由和飞轮都靠可信置信度,校准是它们能正常工作的前提。
optionExplanations_en: Confidence is the core signal for online routing and active learning, not a decorative report number.
Calibration concerns online decision trustworthiness, not training convergence speed.
Confidence can't replace precision/recall; it measures uncertainty, not classification correctness.
Correct — both routing and the flywheel rely on trustworthy confidence, so calibration is the precondition for them to work.

termDefinitions.term: well-calibrated confidence / 良好校准的置信度
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型输出的分数与真实正确概率相符:说 0.7 就约七成正确,可直接用于路由决策。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Well-calibrated confidence means the output score matches the true probability of being correct, so 0.7 is about 70% right and usable for routing.

scenario: 为四个模态各选一个编码器,把原始输入变成定长嵌入。
scenario_en: Pick an encoder per modality to turn raw input into a fixed-dim embedding.
q: 关于四个模态各自的编码器选型,哪些说法是对的？(多选)
q_en: Which statements about the per-modality encoder choices are correct? (multiple)
why: 四路各配专精编码器:文本→多语言 transformer(含 OCR 叠字);图像→ViT/EfficientNet;视频→时序模型;音频→Whisper 转写+声学特征,各自单独微调。
why_en: Text uses a fine-tuned multilingual transformer (mBERT/XLM-R) over captions/comments/OCR text; image uses ViT or EfficientNet; video uses a temporal model (SlowFast/TimeSformer); audio uses Whisper transcription plus a parallel acoustic extractor.
options: 文本:微调的多语言 transformer(mBERT/XLM-R),吃 caption/评论/OCR 出的叠加文字
图像:ViT 或 EfficientNet,检测仇恨符号、裸露、图形暴力
音频:Whisper 转写嵌入 + 并行声学特征提取器(枪声/尖叫)
视频:直接用文本编码器读字幕,不需要任何时序模型
options_en: Text: a fine-tuned multilingual transformer (mBERT/XLM-R) over captions/comments/OCR'd overlay text.
Image: ViT or EfficientNet, detecting hate symbols, nudity, graphic violence.
Audio: Whisper transcription embeddings plus a parallel acoustic extractor (gunshots/distress).
Video: just use the text encoder on subtitles, no temporal model needed.
optionExplanations: 对;一套权重跨语言通用,再加 OCR 后连图上叠字这种纯图像承载的文字也进得来。
对;ViT 或 EfficientNet 都是图像编码主力,按该层的延迟预算在两者间取舍。
对;音频两条线——转写抓口头仇恨,声学抓枪声/尖叫等危险信号。
错;视频的暴力升级/自残步骤是跨帧时序信号,字幕文本抓不到,必须时序模型。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — one set of weights generalizes across languages, and adding OCR pulls in text that only exists baked into an image.
Correct — either ViT or EfficientNet can carry image encoding; the tier latency budget decides which.
Correct — audio has two lines: transcription for spoken hate, acoustics for gunshots/distress.
Wrong — video's escalating violence/self-harm steps are cross-frame temporal signals that subtitles miss, requiring a temporal model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨语言预训练 transformer,一套权重覆盖上百种语言的文本理解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XLM-R (XLM-RoBERTa) is a cross-lingual pretrained transformer whose single set of weights handles text understanding across 100+ languages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把图像切成 patch 序列、用 transformer 编码的视觉模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ViT (Vision Transformer) splits an image into patch tokens and encodes them with a transformer.

termDefinitions.meaning: OpenAI 的语音识别模型,用来把音频转成文本嵌入,供文本层审核。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Whisper is a speech-recognition model used to turn audio into text embeddings for text-layer moderation.

scenario: 很多仇恨内容不是打字发的,而是把文字叠在图片上(meme),或藏在多种语言里。
scenario_en: Much hateful content isn't typed — it's text overlaid on images (memes), or hidden across many languages.
q: 文本编码器该怎么选、吃哪些输入,才不漏掉这类文本？
q_en: How should the text encoder be chosen and what inputs must it consume to not miss such text?
why: 用微调的多语言 transformer(mBERT/XLM-R):一套权重覆盖上百语言,躲进小语种也抓得到。输入不能只吃 caption/评论,还要把图上叠字 OCR 出来一起喂——不然纯图上的仇恨文字就漏了。输出 768 维嵌入。
why_en: Use a fine-tuned multilingual transformer (mBERT/XLM-R) so low-resource languages are still caught, and feed it captions/comments plus OCR'd overlay text or on-image hate text slips through.
tradeoff: 多语言 transformer + OCR(覆盖多语言和图上叠字但更重) vs 单语纯文本模型(轻但漏小语种/叠字)
options: 用单语言词袋模型,只吃打字评论,图上叠字和字幕一概不管
微调多语言 transformer + OCR 叠字一起喂
只用一张脏词正则表匹配拼写变体,不需要训练任何模型
只吃评论区文本,视频字幕和图上叠字全部跳过,不做任何 OCR
options_en: A monolingual bag-of-words model over typed comments only, ignoring on-image text and subtitles.
A fine-tuned multilingual transformer fed captions plus OCR-extracted overlay text.
Just one regex slur list matching spelling variants, with no model to train.
Only comment-section text, skipping video subtitles and on-image text with no OCR at all.
whenOtherWins: 若平台内容确定只有单一语言、纯打字、无图文混排(如某单语纯文字客服系统),一个更轻的单语文本模型就够,不必背多语言+OCR 的成本。
whenOtherWins_en: If the platform is guaranteed single-language, typed-only, with no image-text mixing, a lighter monolingual text model suffices without the multilingual+OCR cost.
optionExplanations: 词袋丢语序和语境,又不覆盖多语言/叠字,躲进小语种或 meme 就漏。
对;跨语言语义在同一嵌入空间里对齐,叠字进模型后 meme 类攻击不再靠纯图像躲过。
脏词正则被拼写变体和语境轻易绕过,还会误伤 counter-speech,不能当主力。
只吃评论会漏掉字幕和图上文字这两大承载,覆盖不全。
optionExplanations_en: Bag-of-words loses word order and context and covers neither multilingual nor overlay text, so low-resource languages or memes slip through.
Correct — cross-lingual meaning lands in one embedding space, and once overlay text is read in, meme-style attacks can no longer hide behind an image.
A slur regex is easily bypassed by spelling variants and context and wrongly flags counter-speech — not a primary encoder.
Comments-only misses subtitles and on-image text, two major carriers, so coverage is incomplete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 光学字符识别:把图片/视频帧里的文字提取成可读文本,供文本编码器处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) extracts text embedded in images/video frames into readable text for the text encoder.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在上百种语言上预训练的 BERT,一套模型处理多语言文本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: mBERT (multilingual BERT) is BERT pretrained on 100+ languages, handling multilingual text with one model.

scenario: 一段视频:每一单帧看都无害,但连起来是暴力在逐步升级/自残的分步演示。
scenario_en: A video where each single frame looks benign, but together they show escalating violence or step-by-step self-harm.
q: 视频编码器该用什么模型,才能抓到这种跨帧的信号？
q_en: What video encoder captures this cross-frame signal?
why: 用时序模型(SlowFast/TimeSformer)在采样关键帧上建模帧间动态——升级、演示步骤这些是跨帧才现形的,任何单帧图像模型都漏。输出 512 维嵌入。逐帧图像分类只能看孤立画面,抓不到'过程'。
why_en: Use a temporal model (SlowFast/TimeSformer) over sampled keyframes to model cross-frame dynamics like escalation, which any single-frame image model misses.
tradeoff: 时序模型(抓跨帧动态但更重) vs 逐帧图像分类(轻但只看孤立帧、漏过程)
options: 对每一帧独立跑图像分类,再取最高分当作整段视频的最终违规分数,不看帧序
只看视频封面缩略图那一张图判定,省下解码和推理算力
时序模型(SlowFast/TimeSformer)建帧间动态
把所有帧拼成一张长图交给 OCR,当纯文本内容来处理
options_en: Classify every frame independently and take the max as the final violation score for the whole video, ignoring frame order.
Judge from the single cover thumbnail to save decoding and inference compute.
A temporal model (SlowFast/TimeSformer) that models cross-frame dynamics.
Stitch all frames into one long image and hand it to OCR as pure text content.
whenOtherWins: 若违规完全体现在单帧(如某一帧出现裸露/血腥),逐帧图像分类就够,不必上时序模型;时序的价值专门在'跨帧才成立'的违规。
whenOtherWins_en: If a violation is fully visible in a single frame (nudity/gore in one frame), per-frame image classification suffices; temporal modeling earns its cost only for cross-frame violations.
optionExplanations: 逐帧取 max 只看孤立画面,升级/演示这种'过程'信号被完全忽略。
单缩略图代表不了整段视频,恶意内容常不在封面。
对;时序模型建模帧间动态,正好抓单帧看不出的升级和分步演示。
拼长图交给 OCR 只处理文字,丢掉画面时序,答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Per-frame max only sees isolated frames, entirely ignoring 'process' signals like escalation/demonstration.
One thumbnail can't represent the whole video, and malicious content often isn't on the cover.
Correct — a temporal model captures inter-frame dynamics, exactly the escalation and step-by-step demos a single frame misses.
Stitching to OCR only handles text and drops visual temporality — off target.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种视频理解网络,用慢/快双通路分别抓语义和运动,建模时序动态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SlowFast is a video network with slow and fast pathways capturing semantics and motion to model temporal dynamics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 transformer 的注意力扩展到时间维度的视频模型,建模帧间关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TimeSformer extends transformer attention to the time dimension to model relationships across video frames.

scenario: 音频里既可能有口头仇恨言论,也可能有枪声、尖叫、人群骚乱这类非语言危险信号。
scenario_en: Audio may carry spoken hate speech and also non-verbal danger cues like gunshots, screams, crowd distress.
q: 音频编码器该怎么设计,才能同时覆盖'说了什么'和'发生了什么声音'？
q_en: How should the audio encoder cover both what was said and what sounds occurred?
why: 两条并行线:Whisper 做语音转写、得到嵌入,交给文本层抓口头仇恨;并行一个声学特征提取器,直接从波形抓枪声/尖叫/人群噪声这些转写抓不到的非语言信号。只做转写会漏掉纯声学的危险。输出 256 维。
why_en: Two parallel lines: Whisper transcription embeddings feed the text layer for spoken hate, and a parallel acoustic extractor catches non-verbal cues like gunshots/screams that transcription misses.
tradeoff: 转写 + 声学双线(覆盖语言与非语言但两套) vs 只转写(简单但漏枪声/尖叫等声学危险)
options: 只做语音转写(Whisper),文字里没有脏词就直接判安全
只做声学事件分类,完全不转写语音说了什么内容
把音频当噪声整段丢掉,只审文本和图像两个模态
Whisper 转写嵌入 + 并行声学特征提取器,两路都覆盖
options_en: Only speech transcription (Whisper); if the transcript has no slurs, mark it safe.
Only acoustic event classification, never transcribing what the speech actually says.
Throw the audio away as noise and moderate just the text and image modalities.
Whisper transcription embeddings plus a parallel acoustic feature extractor, covering both paths.
whenOtherWins: 若平台音频本质只有语音、几乎无环境声(如纯语音客服录音),只做转写就够,声学提取器是多余成本。
whenOtherWins_en: If platform audio is essentially speech-only with negligible ambient sound (voice support recordings), transcription alone suffices and the acoustic extractor is wasted cost.
optionExplanations: 只转写会漏掉枪声/尖叫这类没有'词'的危险声学信号。
只做声学又漏掉了口头仇恨的语义内容,两头都不能少。
丢掉音频等于放弃一整个模态的证据,跨模态攻击正好藏这。
对;转写抓语言、声学抓非语言,两条并行线才把音频证据收全。
optionExplanations_en: Transcription-only misses dangerous acoustic cues like gunshots/screams that have no 'words'.
Acoustic-only misses the semantic content of spoken hate; neither line can be dropped.
Discarding audio abandons a whole modality's evidence, exactly where cross-modal attacks hide.
Correct — transcription captures language and acoustics captures non-verbal, so two parallel lines gather the full audio evidence.

termDefinitions.term: acoustic feature extractor / 声学特征提取器
termDefinitions.meaning: 直接从音频波形提取非语言特征(枪声、尖叫、人群噪声),不依赖转写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An acoustic feature extractor pulls non-verbal features (gunshots, screams, crowd noise) straight from the waveform, independent of transcription.

scenario: 同一个图像编码器,快速 triage 层要求 <50ms,慢速深判层可以给到 200-500ms。
scenario_en: The same image modality: the fast triage tier needs <50ms, while the slow deep tier allows 200-500ms.
q: 编码器深度该怎么选,主要被什么驱动？
q_en: How is encoder depth chosen, and what mainly drives it?
why: 编码器深度 vs 推理延迟是核心取舍,而选多深由所在层的延迟预算决定:快速层用轻量的(如 EfficientNet-B0),慢速层才上重的(如 ViT-Large)。把编码器绑到一个具体延迟数字,比笼统说'用个强模型'专业得多。
why_en: Encoder depth vs inference latency is the core tradeoff, and how deep is driven by the tier's latency budget: a light encoder (EfficientNet-B0) for the fast tier, a heavy one (ViT-Large) for the slow tier.
tradeoff: 深编码器(精度高但慢) vs 浅编码器(快但精度低);由所在层的延迟预算裁决
options: 永远选最深最强的编码器,延迟不重要,精度最高就好
编码器深度由所在层的延迟预算驱动,快层轻、慢层重
深度随便选,反正 fusion 融合层会把精度补齐回来
所有层统一用同一个中等编码器,不区分快慢层预算
options_en: Always take the deepest, strongest encoder; latency does not matter as long as accuracy is highest.
Encoder depth is driven by the tier latency budget — light in the fast tier, heavy in the slow one.
Pick depth arbitrarily; the fusion layer will make the accuracy back up.
Use one medium encoder uniformly in every tier, without separating fast and slow budgets.
whenOtherWins: 若整个系统没有分层、只有一个宽松延迟预算的离线批处理路径,那就可以统一上最深的编码器换最高精度,不必按层分深浅。
whenOtherWins_en: If there's no tiering and only a single loose-budget offline batch path, use the deepest encoder uniformly for max accuracy, without per-tier depth splitting.
optionExplanations: 最深编码器塞进 <50ms 的快速层会超预算,延迟约束真实存在,不能无视。
对;深度是延迟预算的函数,快慢层各配深浅编码器,是标准做法。
fusion 补不回浅编码器丢失的信息,深度得按预算认真选。
统一中等编码器既浪费快速层预算又限死慢速层精度,分层的意义就没了。
optionExplanations_en: The deepest encoder blows a <50ms fast-tier budget; the latency constraint is real and can't be ignored.
Correct — depth is a function of the latency budget, matching light/heavy encoders to fast/slow tiers, the standard practice.
Fusion can't recover information a shallow encoder lost, so depth must be chosen deliberately by budget.
A uniform medium encoder both wastes the fast-tier budget and caps slow-tier accuracy, defeating the point of tiering.

termDefinitions.meaning: EfficientNet 系列里最小最快的一档图像模型,适合快速 triage 层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EfficientNet-B0 is the smallest, fastest tier of the EfficientNet family, fit for the fast triage tier.

scenario: 四个编码器输出维度:文本 768、图像 512、视频 512、音频 256。
scenario_en: Encoder output dims: text 768, image 512, video 512, audio 256.
q: 这些'定长嵌入维度'在架构里起什么作用？
q_en: What role do these fixed-dim embeddings play in the architecture?
why: 维度本身不是考点;关键是每个模态被压成定长向量,才能拼接对齐进 fusion,如 early fusion 拼成约 2048 维再过 MLP。
why_en: The dims themselves aren't the point — each modality becomes a fixed-length vector so it can concatenate into fusion, e.g. early fusion stacks to ~2048 dims.
options: 这是必须硬背的数字,重点是记住 768/512/512/256 这几个具体数值
维度越大精度一定越高,四个都该拉到 768 以上
定长向量让各模态对齐拼接进 fusion,拼成约 2048 维
维度只关乎存储占用,和 fusion 能否运作无关
options_en: These are numbers to memorize by rote — the point is recalling the exact figures 768/512/512/256.
Bigger dims are always more accurate, so push all four above 768.
Fixed-dim vectors let each modality align and concatenate into fusion, stacking to ~2048 dims.
Dims only affect storage footprint, unrelated to whether fusion works.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把任意长度的原始输入压成固定维度的向量,方便下游拼接、对齐、比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fixed-dim embedding compresses variable-length raw input into a constant-size vector for downstream concatenation, alignment, and comparison.

optionExplanations: 把维度当考试要背的数字,忽略了它真正的作用是让各模态向量能互相对齐。
维度不是越大越准,各编码器维度是按模态信息量和延迟预算权衡出的设计选择。
对,重点在'定长'能拼接对齐,不在具体数值大小。
维度不只是存储问题,它决定这个模态的向量能不能被塞进 fusion 层一起处理。
optionExplanations_en: Treating the dims as a memorization target misses their real job of letting modalities align.
Bigger isn't always better — each encoder's dim trades off info content against latency budget, not a race to add size.
Correct — what matters is 'fixed length' enabling concatenation, not the specific numbers.
Dims aren't just about storage; they decide whether this modality's vector can even enter the fusion layer.

scenario: 四路模态嵌入要合并,融合策略直接决定能不能识别跨模态攻击。
scenario_en: The four modality embeddings must merge, and the fusion strategy directly decides cross-modal attack detection.
q: early fusion(拼接+MLP)vs attention-based fusion,核心差别在哪？
q_en: Early fusion (concat + MLP) vs attention-based fusion — what's the core difference?
why: early fusion 拼接过 MLP,快 5-10ms 但把模态当独立、抓不到交互;attention fusion 让模态互相 attend 抓跨模态攻击,代价 +20-50ms。
why_en: Early fusion concatenates then runs an MLP — simple and fast (+5-10ms) but treats modalities independently and misses interactions; attention fusion lets modalities attend to each other and catches cross-modal attacks at +20-50ms and many more params.
tradeoff: early fusion(+5-10ms、弱跨模态) vs attention fusion(+20-50ms、强跨模态)
options: early 拼接过 MLP 快但漏交互;attention 互相 attend 抓交互但更重
两种融合的识别效果和延迟完全一样,只是论文里的命名不同而已
early fusion 比 attention 更能抓跨模态攻击,因为它结构更简单更快
attention fusion 延迟更低也更省参数,应当无脑首选
options_en: Early concatenates through an MLP — fast but misses interaction; attention lets modalities attend to each other, catching interaction but heavier.
The two fusions have identical detection quality and latency; only the names in the papers differ.
Early fusion catches cross-modal attacks better than attention because its structure is simpler and faster.
Attention fusion has lower latency and fewer parameters, so it should be the default choice.
optionExplanations: 对;这正是延迟/参数与跨模态识别力的取舍,快速层用 early、慢速层用 attention。
两者机制与跨模态能力差别很大,效果不等价。
说反了:early 弱在跨模态交互,attention 才强,简单不等于识别力强。
attention 延迟更高不是更低,不能无脑首选,要看层的预算。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — this is exactly the latency/params vs cross-modal-detection tradeoff: early for the fast tier, attention for the slow tier.
Their mechanisms and cross-modal ability differ greatly, so performance isn't equivalent.
Backwards — early is weak on cross-modal interaction; attention is strong, and simple doesn't mean powerful.
Attention has higher, not lower, latency, so it's no no-brainer — it depends on the tier's budget.

termDefinitions.term: cross-modal attention / 跨模态注意力
termDefinitions.meaning: 让每个模态的表示去 attend 其他模态,学出哪些跨模态组合重要,能抓跨模态攻击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-modal attention lets each modality attend to the others, learning which cross-modal combinations matter and catching cross-modal attacks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多层感知机:若干全连接层堆叠的前馈网络,early fusion 用它处理拼接后的嵌入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) is a feed-forward stack of fully connected layers, used by early fusion over the concatenated embeddings.

scenario: 一条内容:图像本身无害、叠加的文字本身也不算太狠,但两者组合起来是明确的仇恨攻击。
scenario_en: An item where the image alone is benign and the overlaid text alone is mild, but their combination is a clear hate attack.
q: 要可靠识别这种组合式跨模态攻击,该用哪种融合？
q_en: Which fusion reliably detects this combinatorial cross-modal attack?
why: 用 attention fusion:跨模态注意力让文字 attend 图像,学出'图+文'组合才是攻击;early fusion 单看都无害就放过。代价 +20-50ms。
why_en: Use attention-based fusion: cross-modal attention lets text attend to image and vice versa, learning that 'this image + this caption' is the attack, whereas early fusion treats them independently and passes both as benign.
tradeoff: attention fusion(抓组合语义但 +20-50ms) vs early fusion(快但把模态当独立、漏组合攻击)
options: late fusion 打分平均,两个模态各自判无害就平均成无害,直接放行
early fusion 拼接+MLP,单看两个模态都无害所以放过
只信图像编码器的判断,文字叠层一概忽略不参与决策
attention fusion:跨模态注意力学出'图+文'组合才是攻击
options_en: Late-fusion score averaging: each modality calls it benign, the average is benign, and it ships.
Early fusion concat plus MLP: both modalities look benign alone, so it passes.
Trust only the image encoder and drop the text overlay out of the decision entirely.
Attention fusion: cross-modal attention learns that image plus text together is the attack.
whenOtherWins: 若攻击其实单模态就成立(图像本身就是血腥/裸露),early 或 late fusion 的快速通道已足够识别,不必付 attention 的延迟成本。
whenOtherWins_en: If the attack is already valid single-modality (the image itself is gore/nudity), the fast early/late path detects it and you needn't pay attention's latency cost.
optionExplanations: late 打分平均没有任何跨模态推理,组合攻击必漏,只配当 baseline。
early 把模态当独立,单看无害就放过,正中组合攻击的盲区。
只看图像直接丢掉文字这一半证据,组合语义无从谈起。
对;跨模态注意力显式建模模态间交互,才抓得住'单看无害、合看有害'的攻击。
optionExplanations_en: Late averaging has no cross-modal reasoning and always misses combinatorial attacks — fit only as a baseline.
Early treats modalities independently and passes both as benign, hitting the combinatorial blind spot.
Image-only discards half the evidence (the text), so combinatorial semantics are impossible.
Correct — cross-modal attention explicitly models inter-modality interaction, catching 'benign alone, harmful together' attacks.

scenario: 团队为了压延迟,全系统只用 early fusion(拼接+MLP),不上任何跨模态注意力。
scenario_en: To cut latency, the team uses only early fusion (concat + MLP) system-wide, with no cross-modal attention anywhere.
q: 全系统只用 early fusion 会有什么后果？
q_en: What's the consequence of using only early fusion system-wide?
why: early fusion 把模态当独立看,对手只要让每个模态单看都无害,组合攻击就系统性绕过。省了 20-50ms,却对整类跨模态对抗内容失明。
why_en: Early fusion treats modalities largely independently, so adversaries keep each modality benign alone and the combinatorial attack systematically bypasses it — saving latency but going blind to a whole class of cross-modal content.
options: 毫无后果,early fusion 和 attention 的识别力其实一样
模态当独立看→组合式跨模态攻击系统性绕过→对整类对抗内容失明
只会略微增加延迟,精度反而比 attention 更高一些
会让音频模态完全失效,但与跨模态组合攻击没有关系
options_en: No consequence at all — early fusion and attention actually detect equally well.
Modalities are treated independently → combinatorial cross-modal attacks bypass systematically → blind to a whole class of adversarial content.
It only slightly raises latency and is in fact a bit more accurate than attention.
It disables the audio modality entirely, but has nothing to do with cross-modal combination attacks.
optionExplanations: early 的跨模态能力明显弱于 attention,识别力并不相同。
对;early 的独立处理正是组合攻击的盲区,慢速层补 attention 才堵得住。
early 延迟更低而非更高,精度在跨模态上反而更弱,选项自相矛盾。
early fusion 不会让音频失效,它的问题是跨模态交互弱,张冠李戴。
optionExplanations_en: Early's cross-modal ability is clearly weaker than attention, so detection isn't the same.
Correct — early's independent handling is the combinatorial blind spot, plugged only by adding attention in the slow tier.
Early has lower, not higher, latency and is weaker on cross-modal, so the option is self-contradictory.
Early fusion doesn't disable audio; its problem is weak cross-modal interaction — a mismatch.

scenario: late fusion(各模态分类器独立打分再平均)延迟最低(+2-5ms),但没有任何跨模态推理。
scenario_en: Late fusion (independent per-modality classifiers averaged) has the lowest latency (+2-5ms) but zero cross-modal reasoning.
q: late fusion 在这套审核架构里该放在什么位置？
q_en: What place does late fusion have in this moderation architecture?
why: 只当 baseline / 降级兜底用,绝不当对抗内容的主力融合。它把每个模态分类器的分数平均,零跨模态推理——组合攻击必漏。它的唯一价值是极低延迟和实现简单,可在主融合超时/故障时兜底。
why_en: Only as a baseline / fallback, never the primary fusion for adversarial content: it averages independent per-modality scores with zero cross-modal reasoning, so combinatorial attacks always slip through.
tradeoff: late fusion(极低延迟但零跨模态) vs attention fusion(高跨模态但更慢);late 只配兜底
options: 当所有对抗内容的主力融合方式,因为它延迟最低最省算力
当唯一的融合方式,彻底取代 early 和 attention 两种
只当 baseline 或降级兜底:零跨模态推理,组合攻击必漏
当 child safety 类别的专用融合,因为它精度最高
options_en: As the primary fusion for all adversarial content, because it has the lowest latency and cheapest compute.
As the only fusion, fully replacing both early and attention fusion.
Only as a baseline or degraded fallback: zero cross-modal reasoning, so combination attacks always slip.
As the dedicated fusion for the child safety category, because it is the most accurate.
whenOtherWins: 若某任务本就是纯单模态(如只审音频转写文本),模态间无交互可言,late fusion 的独立打分就没有劣势,可以正常用。
whenOtherWins_en: If a task is inherently single-modality (moderating only audio transcripts), there's no inter-modal interaction to lose, so late fusion's independent scoring is fine.
optionExplanations: 最快但零跨模态,拿它当对抗主力等于对组合攻击敞开大门。
取代 early/attention 会牺牲全部跨模态识别,方向错了。
对;late 只配当 baseline 或主融合故障时的兜底,不承担对抗内容识别。
late 精度最低而非最高,更不该给最高危的 child safety 用。
optionExplanations_en: Fastest but zero cross-modal; making it the adversarial primary opens the door to combinatorial attacks.
Replacing early/attention sacrifices all cross-modal detection — wrong direction.
Correct — late fits only as a baseline or fallback when the main fusion fails, not for adversarial detection.
Late is the least, not most, accurate, so it's especially wrong for the highest-stakes child safety.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个模态各自分类,再对分数做平均/投票;实现简单但没有跨模态推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Late fusion classifies each modality separately then averages/votes the scores — simple but with no cross-modal reasoning.

scenario: 仇恨言论主要靠文本证据,裸露主要靠图像证据,同一个融合表示要服务多种很不一样的类别。
scenario_en: Hate speech leans on text evidence, nudity on image evidence, and one fused representation must serve many very different categories.
q: 分类头该怎么设计,而不是用一个统一的多分类输出？
q_en: How should the classification heads be designed instead of one unified multi-class output?
why: 每个违规类别一个专属分类头(仇恨/裸露/暴力/垃圾各一个),而不是单一多分类输出。因为不同类别对融合表示的侧重不同——仇恨头更看文本维度,裸露头更看图像维度,各自学不同权重。单一多分类头被迫用一套权重伺候所有类别,细微差别被抹平。
why_en: One dedicated head per harm category (hate/nudity/violence/spam) rather than a single multi-class output, because each head weights the fused representation differently — hate leans on text dims, nudity on image dims.
tradeoff: 类别专属头(各类各学侧重、抓细微差别) vs 单一多分类头(一套权重伺候全类别、抹平差异)
options: 每个违规类别一个专属分类头,各自学不同权重
用一个 softmax 多分类头输出所有类别,一套权重通吃
按模态各建一个分类头,和违规类别本身没有对应关系
只保留一个'违规/安全'二分类头,不区分具体类别
options_en: One dedicated head per harm category, each learning its own weights.
One softmax multi-class head for every category, with a single set of weights covering all of them.
One head per modality, with no correspondence to the harm categories themselves.
Keep only a violating/safe binary head and never distinguish specific categories.
whenOtherWins: 若只有一个粗粒度目标(纯二分类'安全/不安全')、且各类别对证据的侧重几乎一样,单一头更省参数也够用,不必拆多头。
whenOtherWins_en: If there's just one coarse target (plain safe/unsafe) and categories weight evidence almost identically, a single head is cheaper and enough — no need to split.
optionExplanations: 对;类别专属头让每类各学对融合表示的侧重,正好匹配'仇恨靠文本、裸露靠图像'的差异。
单一多分类头用一套权重服务所有类别,抹平了类别间对证据侧重的差异。
按模态设头混淆了'模态'与'违规类别'两个维度,分类目标是类别不是模态。
只留二分类丢掉了类别粒度,没法对不同类别做差异化处置。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — category-specific heads let each learn its own weighting of the fused representation, matching 'hate leans text, nudity leans image'.
One multi-class head serves all categories with one weight set, flattening how categories weight evidence differently.
Per-modality heads conflate 'modality' with 'harm category'; the target is category, not modality.
A binary-only head drops category granularity and can't drive differentiated enforcement per category.

termDefinitions.term: category-specific head / 类别专属分类头
termDefinitions.meaning: 每个违规类别一个独立分类器,各自对共享融合表示学不同的判定权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A category-specific head is a separate classifier per harm category, each learning its own decision weights over the shared fused representation.

scenario: 既想要快速层的低延迟,又想要慢速层能抓跨模态攻击,两种融合各有代价。
scenario_en: You want the fast tier's low latency and the slow tier's cross-modal detection, but each fusion has a cost.
q: 两种融合怎么和分层配合,才能兼得速度与识别力？
q_en: How do the two fusions pair with the tiers to get both speed and detection?
why: 快速 triage 层用 early fusion(+5-10ms,够判明显内容),慢速深判层用 attention fusion(+20-50ms 只花在少量难件上)。
why_en: The compromise: concatenation (early fusion) in the fast triage tier, attention fusion in the slow deep tier, so the majority takes the cheap path and only hard items pay for cross-modal reasoning.
options: 快速 triage 层用 attention fusion,慢速深判层反而用 early fusion,两者位置对调
两层都用 attention fusion,不计延迟只求最高识别力,总成本直接翻倍
快速层用 early fusion,慢速深判层用 attention fusion
两层都用 late fusion 打分平均,虽最省延迟但两层都测不出跨模态组合攻击
options_en: The fast triage tier uses attention fusion while the slow deep tier uses early fusion instead — the two positions are swapped.
Attention fusion in both tiers, ignoring latency and chasing only the highest detection power, doubling total cost.
Early fusion in the fast tier, attention fusion in the slow deep tier.
Late-fusion score averaging in both tiers — cheapest on latency, but neither tier can catch cross-modal combination attacks.
optionExplanations: 把 attention 放快速层会撑爆 <50ms 预算,顺序反了。
两层都 attention 会把昂贵推理浪费在绝大多数明显内容上,成本失控。
对;便宜的 early 处理多数、昂贵的 attention 只伺候少量难件,正是分层的意义。
两层都 late 就彻底放弃跨模态识别,慢速层白搭。
optionExplanations_en: Putting attention in the fast tier blows the <50ms budget — the order is reversed.
Attention in both wastes expensive reasoning on the vast majority of obvious content, blowing up cost.
Correct — cheap early handles the majority and expensive attention serves only the few hard items, exactly the point of tiering.
Late in both abandons cross-modal detection entirely, wasting the slow tier.

scenario: 绝大多数内容要么明显安全、要么明显违规,只有一小部分是真正模糊的;但深度多模态管线每条要 200-500ms。
scenario_en: Most content is clearly safe or clearly violating, only a small fraction is genuinely ambiguous, yet the deep multimodal pipeline costs 200-500ms per item.
q: 面对这种内容分布,该怎么组织推理,而不是每条都跑深度管线？
q_en: Given this content distribution, how do you organize inference instead of running the deep pipeline on everything?
why: 用分层集成利用分布:轻量 Tier 1 在 <50ms 内自动搞定 85-95% 明显内容,只有 5-15% 不确定的升级到 Tier 2(200-500ms)。
why_en: Exploit the distribution with a tiered ensemble: a light Tier-1 triage (<50ms) auto-handles the 85-95% obvious items, and only the uncertain 5-15% escalate to the heavy Tier-2 deep pipeline (200-500ms).
tradeoff: 分层集成(多数走便宜层、难件才上重层) vs 全量跑深管线(精度均匀但成本×10-20)
options: 每条内容都跑完整深度多模态管线(200-500ms),保证最高精度但不做任何分流,成本翻十几倍
只跑快速层(<50ms),永远不升级到深度管线,用精度损失换算力成本
随机一半走快速层、一半走深度层,分流概率和内容本身的难易完全无关
分层集成:Tier 1 自动处理 85-95%,只有 5-15% 升级
options_en: Run the full deep multimodal pipeline (200-500ms) on every item for uniform top accuracy, with no routing at all — cost balloons to over 10x.
Run only the fast tier (<50ms) and never escalate to the deep pipeline, trading accuracy loss for compute cost.
Send half at random to the fast tier and half to the deep tier — the split has nothing to do with how hard the content actually is.
Tiered ensemble: Tier 1 auto-handles 85-95%, and only the uncertain 5-15% escalate.
whenOtherWins: 若内容量很小、且几乎每条都难判(如专门的高危小众平台),分层带来的算力节省不明显,全量走深管线换最高一致精度反而更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: If volume is tiny and nearly every item is hard (a specialized high-risk niche platform), tiering saves little and running the deep pipeline on all for uniform accuracy fits better.
optionExplanations: 全量深管线把 200-500ms 均摊到明显内容上,成本是分层的十几倍,规模上不可行。
只跑快速层会漏掉需要深判的难件,精度在边界上塌陷。
随机分流不看难易,难件可能走了快速层被误判,浪费了深层。
对;按'明显 vs 模糊'分布分流,便宜层扛多数、重层专攻少数难件,是标准分层解。
optionExplanations_en: The full deep pipeline spreads 200-500ms over obvious content, costing 10x+ of tiering — infeasible at scale.
Fast-tier-only misses hard items that need deep classification, collapsing accuracy at the border.
Random splitting ignores difficulty, so hard items may take the fast tier and be misjudged, wasting the deep tier.
Correct — routing by the obvious-vs-ambiguous distribution lets the cheap tier carry the majority and the heavy tier focus on the few hard items — the standard tiered solution.

scenario: Tier 1 要在 <50ms 内给绝大多数内容一个决定,只有高置信的才自动处置。
scenario_en: Tier 1 must decide most content within <50ms, auto-acting only on high-confidence items.
q: Tier 1 快速 triage 该用什么样的模型？
q_en: What kind of model should the Tier-1 fast triage use?
why: 用轻量模型:文本 n-gram 上的逻辑回归、小 CNN、或蒸馏过的编码器,压进 <50ms。高置信(高于上阈或低于下阈)的直接自动决策,搞定 85-95% 内容。它不追求最高精度,只追求'便宜且对明显内容够准'。
why_en: Use lightweight models — logistic regression on text n-grams, a small CNN, or distilled encoders — under 50ms, auto-deciding high-confidence items to clear 85-95% of content cheaply.
tradeoff: 轻量 Tier 1(便宜、覆盖多数明显内容) vs 重模型放前(准但撑爆 <50ms 预算)
options: 用完整 attention 多模态管线,精度优先,不管延迟预算
轻量模型(n-gram LR/小 CNN/蒸馏编码器),<50ms
用最大的 ViT-Large + 时序视频模型,越重越准越好
不用模型,先让人工把每条内容都过一遍再入库
options_en: The full attention multimodal pipeline, accuracy first, ignoring the latency budget.
Lightweight models (n-gram LR / small CNN / distilled encoders) under 50ms.
The biggest ViT-Large plus a temporal video model — heavier is always more accurate.
No model at all; have humans review every item before anything is stored.
whenOtherWins: 若某高危类别(child safety)连'明显安全'都不敢让轻量模型自动放行,那这类内容应跳过 Tier 1 自动决策、直接进人工/重模型,轻量 triage 不适用。
whenOtherWins_en: If a high-risk category (child safety) can't trust a light model to even auto-clear 'obviously safe', it should skip Tier-1 auto-decision and go straight to humans/heavy models.
optionExplanations: 完整 attention 管线要 200-500ms,塞进 <50ms 的 Tier 1 直接超预算。
对;轻量模型在 <50ms 内对明显内容够准,自动扛下 85-95%,把难件留给 Tier 2。
最重的模型是 Tier 2 的活,放在快速层会撑爆延迟预算。
全人工先过在数十亿量级下产能崩溃,Tier 1 的意义正是自动化。
optionExplanations_en: The full attention pipeline needs 200-500ms and blows the <50ms Tier-1 budget outright.
Correct — light models are accurate enough on obvious content within 50ms, auto-clearing 85-95% and leaving hard items to Tier 2.
The heaviest models are Tier 2's job; in the fast tier they blow the latency budget.
Human-first at billions collapses throughput; Tier 1's whole point is automation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用知识蒸馏把大编码器压成更小更快的版本,精度略降但适合低延迟层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distilled encoder is a smaller, faster version of a large encoder via knowledge distillation, trading a little accuracy for low-latency serving.

scenario: Tier 1 <50ms 处理约 85-95% 内容;剩下约 5-15% 走 Tier 2,每条 200-500ms。
scenario_en: Tier 1 at <50ms handles ~85-95% of content; the remaining ~5-15% goes to Tier 2 at 200-500ms each.
q: 这组分层比例和延迟数字,对成本设计意味着什么？
q_en: What do these tier split ratios and latency numbers imply for cost design?
why: 这些是经验量级,不是公式:多数内容明显,走 <50ms 便宜层;少数难件才付 200-500ms。总成本≈便宜层×全量+贵层×少量,被这个约 10x 差值压低。
why_en: Empirical orders of magnitude, not a formula: most content is obvious and takes the cheap <50ms tier, only the hard fraction pays 200-500ms, so total cost is pulled down by roughly that 10x gap.
options: 这只是要背的数字,考点是记住 85-95% 和 200-500ms
既然只慢一点,不如全量都走 Tier 2 更省心
多数内容明显→走便宜层;少数难件→付重成本,总算力被这个量级差压低
既然多数很明显,Tier 1 就没用了,该全量上 Tier 2
options_en: These are numbers to memorize — the point is recalling 85-95% and 200-500ms.
Since it's only a bit slower, just run everything through Tier 2.
Most content is obvious and takes the cheap tier; only hard items pay the heavy cost, pulling total compute down.
Since most content is obvious, Tier 1 is pointless — run everything through Tier 2.

termDefinitions.meaning: 各层处理内容的比例(如 Tier1 85-95%、Tier2 5-15%),决定总算力成本结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The tier split is the share of content each tier handles (e.g. Tier1 85-95%, Tier2 5-15%), setting the total compute cost structure.

optionExplanations: 死记数字没用,关键是理解这组比例怎么压低总成本。
'只慢一点'算错了账,200-500ms 乘以全量比乘以 5-15% 贵了近十倍。
对,便宜层扛住大部分明显内容,总成本才没被少数难件的高延迟拖垮。
说反了,正因多数内容明显,Tier 1 才该先兜底,把算力全砸进 Tier 2 反而浪费。
optionExplanations_en: Memorizing the numbers misses the point — what matters is how this ratio drives down total cost.
'Only a bit slower' misjudges the math — paying 200-500ms on all volume costs nearly 10x more than on just 5-15%.
Correct — the cheap tier absorbs most obvious content, so total cost isn't dragged down by the few hard items' latency.
Backwards — because most content is obvious, Tier 1 should catch it first; routing everything through Tier 2 wastes compute.

scenario: 从 Tier 1 升级上来的 5-15% 不确定内容,可以接受 200-500ms 的处理时间。
scenario_en: The 5-15% uncertain content escalated from Tier 1 can tolerate 200-500ms.
q: Tier 2 深判层该用什么配置来伺候这些难件？
q_en: What configuration should the Tier-2 deep tier use for these hard items?
why: 只有 5-15% 走这层,所以敢上重编码器(ViT-Large/SlowFast)+ attention fusion,吃满 200-500ms 换精度。
why_en: Use the full multimodal pipeline: heavy encoders (ViT-Large, SlowFast) plus attention fusion, spending 200-500ms for much higher accuracy, affordable because only 5-15% pass through.
tradeoff: Tier 2 重管线(高精度但 200-500ms,只用于少量难件) vs 继续用轻量(省时但漏难件)
options: 重编码器(ViT-Large/SlowFast)+ attention fusion
还是用 Tier 1 的轻量 n-gram 逻辑回归,只是多跑几遍取平均分,指望多数投票能补精度
直接把这 5-15% 全部送人工复审,跳过模型判断,想靠人力兜底难件
用 late fusion 对各模态打分独立取平均,不做联合建模,图快省算力
options_en: Heavy encoders (ViT-Large/SlowFast) plus attention fusion.
Still Tier 1's lightweight n-gram logistic regression, just run it several times and average the scores, hoping majority voting makes up the accuracy.
Send all of that 5-15% straight to human review, skip model judgment entirely, and rely on people to backstop the hard items.
Use late-fusion score averaging across modalities independently, with no joint modeling, just to get a faster result and save compute.
whenOtherWins: 若某条难件即便 Tier 2 深判后仍不确定,才轮到送人工复审——人工是 Tier 2 之后的最后一层,不是替代 Tier 2 的模型。
whenOtherWins_en: Only when an item stays uncertain after Tier-2 deep classification does it go to human review — humans are the layer after Tier 2, not a replacement for it.
optionExplanations: 对;难件值得付重编码器+attention 的成本,且只占 5-15%,总成本可控。
重复跑轻量模型不会凭空变准,难件需要的是更强的表达力,不是多跑几遍。
全送人工把 5-15% 的量压给人力,产能扛不住,人工只该接 Tier 2 后仍不确定的。
late fusion 零跨模态推理,恰恰漏掉难件里的组合攻击,和 Tier 2 的目标相悖。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — hard items are worth the heavy-encoder + attention cost and are only 5-15%, keeping total cost manageable.
Re-running a light model doesn't make it accurate; hard items need more expressive power, not more passes.
All-to-humans dumps the 5-15% volume on headcount that can't cope; humans should only take items still uncertain after Tier 2.
Late fusion has zero cross-modal reasoning and misses exactly the combinatorial attacks in hard items, opposing Tier 2's goal.

scenario: Tier 1 对每条内容输出一个校准过的违规概率;要定一条规则决定哪些升级到 Tier 2。
scenario_en: Tier 1 outputs a calibrated violation probability per item; you need a rule for which escalate to Tier 2.
q: 该按什么规则把内容从 Tier 1 升级到 Tier 2？
q_en: By what rule should content escalate from Tier 1 to Tier 2?
why: 用不确定带:概率落在中间带(如 0.3-0.7)升级到 Tier 2,高/低置信留在 Tier 1 自动处置。带宽按类别单独调,且依赖 Tier 1 校准。
why_en: Use an uncertainty band: items whose predicted probability falls in the middle (e.g. 0.3-0.7) escalate to Tier 2, while high-confidence items above/below the thresholds are auto-handled in Tier 1.
tradeoff: 不确定带升级(把难件送 Tier 2) vs 固定比例/随机升级(不看置信度、错送难易件)
options: 按内容长度升级:长文本和长视频一律送 Tier 2 深判
固定把每条内容的前 10% 升级,完全不看置信度
预测概率落在中间不确定带(如 0.3-0.7)的升级
随机抽 5-15% 升级,和模型输出的概率无关
options_en: Escalate by content length: long text and long video always go to Tier 2 deep classification.
Always escalate a fixed top 10% of items, without looking at confidence at all.
Items whose predicted probability lands in the middle uncertainty band (say 0.3-0.7) escalate.
Escalate a random 5-15%, unrelated to the probability the model outputs.
whenOtherWins: 对 child safety,即便预测概率不在中间带、看起来'高置信安全',也可能要强制升级复核——这时不是按带宽,而是按类别策略覆盖路由。
whenOtherWins_en: For child safety, even items outside the band that look 'high-confidence safe' may be force-escalated for review — routing is overridden by category policy, not band width.
optionExplanations: 内容长度与违规不确定性无关,长短不是升级依据。
固定前 10% 不看置信度,可能把明显内容送上去、把真难件漏在下面。
对;中间带正是模型最不确定处,把这批送 Tier 2 深判,高置信的省算力自动处置。
随机升级不区分难易,难件照样被 Tier 1 误判,浪费 Tier 2 产能。
optionExplanations_en: Content length is unrelated to violation uncertainty; length isn't an escalation basis.
A fixed top 10% ignores confidence and may escalate obvious items while leaving truly hard ones below.
Correct — the middle band is where the model is least certain, so escalate it to Tier 2 while auto-handling high-confidence items cheaply.
Random escalation ignores difficulty, so hard items are still misjudged by Tier 1, wasting Tier 2 capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率的一段中间区间(如 0.3-0.7),落入者被判为模糊、升级到更强的层或人工。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The uncertainty band is a middle range of predicted probability (e.g. 0.3-0.7); items inside are deemed ambiguous and escalated to a stronger tier or humans.

scenario: 不确定带的宽窄(比如 0.4-0.6 vs 0.2-0.8)是可调的,直接改变升级到 Tier 2 的量。
scenario_en: The band width (e.g. 0.4-0.6 vs 0.2-0.8) is tunable and directly changes how much escalates to Tier 2.
q: 把不确定带调窄 vs 调宽,分别有什么后果？
q_en: What are the consequences of narrowing vs widening the uncertainty band?
why: 窄带升级少,Tier 2 负载低、成本省,但更多边界内容被 Tier 1 直接自动判错;宽带升级多,精度高但算力贵。带宽是精度 vs 成本的旋钮。
why_en: Narrow band → fewer escalate → lower Tier-2 load and cost but more borderline auto-decided by Tier 1, so more borderline errors; wide band → more escalate → higher accuracy but more Tier-2 compute.
tradeoff: 窄带(省 Tier 2 成本但边界错多) vs 宽带(精度高但 Tier 2 算力大)
options: 窄带和宽带的效果其实一样,只是阈值数字不同而已
窄带会升级更多条、Tier 2 成本更高;宽带升级更少、成本更低
带宽只影响单条延迟,不影响精度也不影响成本
窄带→升级少→省成本但边界错多;宽带→升级多→精度高但算力贵
options_en: Narrow and wide bands behave the same; only the threshold numbers differ.
A narrow band escalates more items and costs more in Tier 2; a wide band escalates fewer and costs less.
Band width only affects per-item latency, not accuracy and not cost.
Narrow → fewer escalations → cheaper but more borderline errors; wide → more escalations → better accuracy but pricier compute.
optionExplanations: 两者在成本/精度上明显不同,不是数字游戏。
说反了:窄带升级更少、成本更省;宽带升级更多、成本更高。
带宽同时牵动精度和成本,不只是延迟,遗漏了核心权衡。
对;带宽是精度 vs 成本的旋钮,按类别非对称成本拧宽或拧窄。
optionExplanations_en: The two differ clearly in cost/accuracy — not a numbers game.
Backwards — a narrow band escalates fewer and costs less; a wide band escalates more and costs more.
Band width moves both accuracy and cost, not just latency, missing the core tradeoff.
Correct — band width is the accuracy-vs-cost knob, widened or narrowed by each category's asymmetric cost.

scenario: 同一套分层系统里,child safety 和 spam 用同一个不确定带宽度似乎不太对。
scenario_en: In the same tiered system, using one band width for both child safety and spam feels wrong.
q: 不确定带宽度该按什么来定,child safety 和 spam 该一样吗？
q_en: What sets the band width, and should child safety and spam share one?
why: 按类别的非对称成本来定,不该一刀切。child safety 漏放代价极端,要用很宽的带(多升级、多复核、宁可多花算力也别漏);spam 漏一条代价低,可以用窄带、多自动处置省算力。带宽是每类的策略旋钮。
why_en: Set band width by each category's asymmetric cost, not one-size-fits-all: child safety uses a much wider band (escalate more, never miss) while spam uses a narrow band to auto-handle more and save compute.
tradeoff: child safety 宽带(宁多算力不漏放) vs spam 窄带(省算力、容忍偶发漏放)
options: child safety 用比 spam 宽得多的带,按漏放代价定
所有类别统一用一个带宽,简单一致最好维护也最好解释
spam 用比 child safety 更宽的带,因为垃圾内容量更大
带宽按内容语言定,和违规类别的代价无关
options_en: Child safety uses a much wider band than spam, set by the cost of a miss.
One band width for every category — simple, consistent, easiest to maintain and explain.
Spam uses a wider band than child safety because there is far more spam by volume.
Band width is set by the content language, unrelated to the cost of the harm category.
whenOtherWins: 若某低危类别的人工/算力预算极紧张,即便理论上想加宽,也可能被迫收窄带、接受更多自动处置——这时预算约束压过纯风险考量。
whenOtherWins_en: If a low-risk category's human/compute budget is extremely tight, you may be forced to narrow the band and accept more auto-decisions, with budget overriding pure risk.
optionExplanations: 对;非对称成本高的类别(child safety)拧宽带多升级,低危(spam)拧窄带省算力。
统一带宽忽略了类别间成本天差地别,child safety 和 spam 不该同等对待。
说反了:spam 漏放代价低该用窄带,child safety 才该用宽带,量大不是理由。
带宽由危害成本决定,不是内容语言,张冠李戴。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — high asymmetric-cost categories (child safety) widen the band to escalate more, while low-risk ones (spam) narrow it to save compute.
One band width ignores that per-category costs differ hugely; child safety and spam shouldn't be treated equally.
Backwards — spam's low miss cost warrants a narrow band and child safety a wide one; volume isn't the reason.
Band width is set by harm cost, not content language — a mismatch.

scenario: 面试官问:Tier 1 快速 triage 层在整套系统里最核心的目的是什么？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: what is the primary purpose of the Tier-1 fast triage in the whole system?
q: Tier 1 的首要目的是什么？
q_en: What is the primary purpose of Tier 1?
why: 首要目的是用低延迟、高置信的自动决策扛下绝大多数内容量(85-95%),把昂贵的 Tier 2 和人工留给少数真正难判的。它不是为了追求单条最高精度,而是为了在规模上把成本压下来、只让难件消耗重资源。
why_en: To handle the majority of content volume at low latency with high-confidence automated decisions, freeing the expensive Tier 2 and humans for the small hard fraction.
options: 用低延迟高置信自动决策扛下绝大多数内容量
对每条内容都做到最高精度,直接取代 Tier 2
只负责收集数据和打日志,不做任何处置决策
专门处理最难、最模糊的那批边界内容
options_en: Absorb the bulk of content volume with low-latency, high-confidence automated decisions.
Reach top accuracy on every single item and replace Tier 2 outright.
Only collect data and write logs, making no enforcement decision.
Handle specifically the hardest, most ambiguous borderline content.
optionExplanations: 对;Tier 1 的价值在低延迟高吞吐地清掉多数明显内容,不是追单条极致精度。
追单条最高精度是 Tier 2 的定位,Tier 1 追的是规模与成本。
Tier 1 对高置信内容是真的在做自动决策,不只是收数据。
最难最模糊的边界内容恰恰是升级给 Tier 2 的,不是 Tier 1 处理的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — Tier 1's value is clearing most obvious content at low latency and high throughput, not maxing per-item accuracy.
Max per-item accuracy is Tier 2's role; Tier 1 targets scale and cost.
Tier 1 genuinely makes automated decisions on high-confidence content, not just data collection.
The hardest, most ambiguous content is precisely what escalates to Tier 2, not what Tier 1 handles.

scenario: Tier 2 对每条难件输出一个置信度分数;这个分数除了做即时决策,还能派别的用场。
scenario_en: Tier 2 outputs a confidence score per hard item; beyond the immediate decision, that score can serve another purpose.
q: Tier 2 输出的置信度,除了当下决策还该用来做什么？
q_en: Beyond the immediate decision, what else should Tier 2's confidence be used for?
why: 双重用途:(1)即时路由决策——够高置信就自动处置;(2)挑主动学习候选——即便过了 Tier 2 仍不确定的,按不确定度排序进人工队列,标注后回炉训练。同一个置信度既驱动当下决策,又喂养飞轮。
why_en: Dual purpose: (1) the immediate routing decision, and (2) selecting active-learning candidates — items still uncertain after Tier 2 go to the human queue ordered by uncertainty, then back into training.
tradeoff: 置信度双用(决策 + 主动学习选样) vs 只用于决策(浪费了免费的选样信号)
options: 只用来做当下这一次路由决策,用完就丢弃,不再留存供其他用途
用来决定这条视频该用什么编码格式和码率,和置信度的设计目的无关
当主动学习的样本选择信号,按不确定度排人工队列
用来给用户主页展示一个公开的信任分数,暴露内部审核信号
options_en: Only for this one immediate routing decision, then discarded and never kept for anything else.
To decide what codec and bitrate this video should use — unrelated to what confidence is for.
As the active-learning sample-selection signal, queueing humans by uncertainty.
To display a public trust score on the user profile, exposing an internal moderation signal.
whenOtherWins: 若模型已经很成熟、飞轮几乎榨不出新增益,可以只用置信度做决策、暂停主动学习采样,把人力挪去别处——但这是成熟期的特例。
whenOtherWins_en: If the model is very mature and the flywheel yields little new gain, you may use confidence only for decisions and pause AL sampling — a late-stage exception.
optionExplanations: 用完即弃浪费了一个免费的高价值信号:最不确定的样本正是最值得标的。
编码格式与置信度毫无关系,是无关项。
对;同一置信度既做决策又挑最不确定样本喂飞轮,是 Tier 2 分数的双重价值。
给用户看信任分不是这里的设计目的,也不解决模型改进。
optionExplanations_en: Discarding it wastes a free high-value signal: the most uncertain items are exactly the most worth labeling.
Codec has nothing to do with confidence — an irrelevant option.
Correct — the same confidence both decides and selects the most uncertain items for the flywheel, Tier 2's dual value.
Showing users a trust score isn't the design goal here and doesn't improve the model.

q: 把内容审核的五步主动学习飞轮排成正确顺序:
q_en: Order the five-step content-moderation active-learning flywheel:
steps: 模型分类:集成在各层输出校准置信度
不确定性路由:低置信的 Tier 2 项按不确定度排入人工队列
人工标注:按政策 taxonomy 标注,靠 IAA 保证质量
增量重训:用新标签更新模型在它吃力的样例上
新不确定前沿:重训后的模型 surface 出新一批不确定项,循环
why: 闭环:模型打分 → 低置信项按不确定度路由人工 → 人工标注 → 增量重训 → 新前沿再 surface 出不确定项。每转一圈,模型在原本吃力处变强,又暴露下一批难件。白板上一定要画出人工复审回到训练管线的反馈箭头。
why_en: The loop: model scores, low-confidence items route to humans by uncertainty, humans label, incremental retrain, and a new frontier surfaces fresh uncertain items — draw the feedback arrow from review back to training.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["模型分类
校准置信度"] --> B["不确定性路由"] B --> C["人工标注
IAA 质量"] C --> D["增量重训"] D --> E["新不确定前沿"] E --> A

termDefinitions.term: active-learning flywheel / 主动学习飞轮
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型打分→路由不确定项→人工标注→重训→新前沿的自我强化闭环,持续改进模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The active-learning flywheel is the self-reinforcing loop of scoring, routing uncertain items, labeling, retraining, and a new frontier, continually improving the model.

scenario: 一个重训好的集成模型置信度没校准好就上线,直接拿它的分数决定'哪些内容进人工队列'。
scenario_en: A retrained ensemble ships with poorly calibrated confidence and uses its scores to decide which items enter the human queue.
q: 校准是这套架构的命门。校准差会引发什么后果链？
q_en: Calibration is the linchpin here — what consequence chain does poor calibration trigger?
why: 校准差 → 模型说的'不确定'不是真不确定 → 路由把错的内容送人工(简单件占满审核产能、真正模糊的反而被自动误判)→ 宝贵人力浪费、飞轮学到的是错样本 → 整个循环退化。所以任何重训模型上线前必须在留出校准集上验证校准。
why_en: Poor calibration means 'uncertain' isn't truly uncertain, so routing sends the wrong items to humans — easy ones clog reviewer capacity while genuinely ambiguous ones get auto-misjudged — wasting people and degrading the flywheel.
options: 校准无所谓,只要集成精度够高,路由自然就正确
校准差只影响离线指标,对线上人工队列没有影响
送错内容进人工队列→浪费人力+飞轮学错→循环退化
校准只决定推理速度快慢,和路由质量没有关系
options_en: Calibration does not matter; if ensemble accuracy is high, routing comes out right anyway.
Bad calibration only hurts offline metrics and leaves the live human queue untouched.
Wrong items enter the human queue → wasted reviewers plus a flywheel trained on bad samples → the loop degrades.
Calibration only sets inference speed and has nothing to do with routing quality.
optionExplanations: 精度高但置信度不可信,照样把错的内容路由进队列,校准是路由的前提。
校准差直接改变'谁进人工队列',线上影响非常实,不只是离线数字。
对;校准是路由命门,坏校准让人力浪费在简单件、放过真模糊,飞轮学错样本、循环退化。
校准影响的是置信度可信度和路由质量,不是推理速度。
optionExplanations_en: High accuracy with untrustworthy confidence still routes wrong items into the queue; calibration is the precondition for routing.
Poor calibration directly changes who enters the human queue — a very real online effect, not just offline numbers.
Correct — calibration is the routing linchpin; bad calibration wastes people on easy items, lets true ambiguity through, and the flywheel learns wrong samples, degrading the loop.
Calibration affects confidence trustworthiness and routing quality, not inference speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一份留出数据,专门用来验证模型输出的置信度是否与真实正确率相符,上线前必查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A calibration set is held-out data used to verify that output confidence matches true correctness before shipping.

scenario: 白板上画审核系统时,面试官特别想看到某一条箭头。
scenario_en: While whiteboarding the moderation system, the interviewer specifically wants to see one particular arrow.
q: 白板设计审核系统时,最该画出哪条箭头,为什么？
q_en: When whiteboarding the moderation system, which arrow must you draw, and why?
why: 画出从人工复审回到训练管线的反馈箭头:它把系统从'静态部署'变成'闭环持续学习'。面试官想看到闭环——新标签回流重训,模型追上演进的政策和新违规,而不是一次训练永久部署。
why_en: Draw the feedback arrow from human review back to the training pipeline, turning a static deployment into a closed continual-learning loop that keeps up with evolving policy.
options: 从人工复审回到训练管线的反馈箭头
从 CDN 到用户浏览器的内容分发箭头
从数据库到监控面板的指标读取箭头
从负载均衡器到后端服务器的转发箭头
options_en: The feedback arrow from human review back into the training pipeline.
The delivery arrow from the CDN to the user browser.
The metrics read arrow from the database to the monitoring dashboard.
The forwarding arrow from the load balancer to the backend servers.
optionExplanations: 对;反馈箭头体现闭环学习,是审核系统对抗政策演进的关键,面试官专门在找它。
CDN 分发是内容交付,与审核模型的学习闭环无关。
监控读取是可观测性,不构成'人工标签回流训练'的闭环。
负载均衡转发是流量层,和持续学习闭环无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the feedback arrow embodies closed-loop learning, the key to keeping up with evolving policy, and interviewers look for it specifically.
CDN delivery is content transport, unrelated to the moderation model's learning loop.
Monitoring reads are observability, not the 'human labels back into training' loop.
Load-balancer forwarding is the traffic layer, unrelated to the continual-learning loop.

scenario: 三种融合的延迟开销:late 打分平均 +2-5ms,early 拼接+MLP +5-10ms,attention 跨模态 +20-50ms。
scenario_en: Fusion latency costs: late averaging +2-5ms, early concat+MLP +5-10ms, attention cross-modal +20-50ms.
q: 这组融合延迟数字,该怎么指导分层里的融合选型？
q_en: How should these fusion-latency numbers guide fusion choice across tiers?
why: 这些是经验量级,不是公式:attention 比 early 贵约 4-5 倍延迟,只配花在少量难件;快速层用 early 的 +5-10ms,难件才上 attention 的 +20-50ms。
why_en: Empirical orders of magnitude, not a formula: attention costs ~4-5x early's latency, worth paying only for the few hard items — the fast tier uses early's +5-10ms, and only hard items get attention's +20-50ms.
options: 这组数字要死记,考点是背出 +2-5/+5-10/+20-50ms
attention 延迟最低,所有层都该无脑上它
attention 比 early 贵 4-5 倍延迟,只留给少量难件
三种融合延迟差异太小可忽略,随便放哪层都行
options_en: Memorize this set — the point is reciting +2-5/+5-10/+20-50ms.
Attention has the lowest latency, so use it everywhere without thinking.
Attention costs ~4-5x early's latency, worth paying only for the few hard items.
The latency gaps between the three are negligible, so any fusion fits any tier.

termDefinitions.term: fusion latency budget / 融合延迟预算
termDefinitions.meaning: 各层可分配给融合步骤的延迟额度,决定该层用便宜的 early/late 还是昂贵的 attention。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The fusion latency budget is the per-tier latency allotted to the fusion step, deciding cheap early/late vs expensive attention.

optionExplanations: 死记数字没意义,重点是这组倍数怎么决定该把哪种融合放哪一层。
说反了,attention 是三者里最贵的,不是最低延迟,无脑首选会撑爆快速层预算。
对,4-5 倍的差价只值得花在少数难件,便宜的 early 留给绝大多数明显内容。
差异并不小,从 +5-10ms 到 +20-50ms 是数倍差距,直接决定分层怎么配。
optionExplanations_en: Memorizing the numbers misses the point — what matters is how this ratio decides which fusion goes in which tier.
Backwards — attention is the most expensive of the three, not the lowest latency; using it everywhere blows the fast tier's budget.
Correct — the 4-5x premium is worth paying only for the few hard items, leaving cheap early to handle the rest.
The gap isn't small — going from +5-10ms to +20-50ms is several times larger and directly decides tier placement.

scenario: 面试里你说'图像用一个强的视觉模型',面试官追问:具体哪个、在哪一层、多少延迟？
scenario_en: In the interview you say 'use a strong vision model for images'; the interviewer probes: which one, in which tier, at what latency?
q: 描述编码器选型时,怎么说才显专业？
q_en: How should you describe encoder choices to sound senior?
why: 把每个编码器绑到一个具体延迟数字和所在层:'快速 triage 用 EfficientNet-B0、慢速深判用 ViT-Large',远胜于笼统说'用个强模型'。这直接体现你懂编码器深度 vs 延迟的取舍是被每层预算驱动的,而不是空谈精度。
why_en: Tie each encoder to a concrete latency number and its tier — 'EfficientNet-B0 in the fast tier, ViT-Large in the slow tier' — beating a vague 'use a strong model'.
tradeoff: 绑具体模型+延迟+所在层(显示懂预算取舍) vs 笼统'用个强模型'(听不出工程判断)
options: 把编码器绑到具体延迟和所在层来说
只说'用最先进的多模态大模型',不提延迟和层
说'哪个都行,fusion 会补齐',回避选型问题
只报参数量最大的那个模型,越大越显专业
options_en: Tie each encoder to a concrete latency number and the tier it sits in.
Just say "use a state-of-the-art multimodal large model" with no latency and no tier.
Say "any of them works, fusion makes up for it" and dodge the choice.
Name only the model with the most parameters — bigger sounds more senior.
whenOtherWins: 在最早的问题框定阶段、还没确定延迟预算时,可以先笼统说'需要一个视觉编码器',等预算和分层定了再落到具体型号——那时空泛是合理的占位。
whenOtherWins_en: At the earliest framing stage before the latency budget is set, a vague 'we'll need a vision encoder' is a fair placeholder until budget and tiers are pinned.
optionExplanations: 对;具体型号+延迟+所在层直接展示你按预算做编码器取舍的工程判断。
'最先进大模型'不落到延迟和层,听不出你懂分层预算,是空话。
'哪个都行'回避了核心取舍,fusion 补不回编码器丢的信息。
只报最大参数量忽视了延迟预算,大模型塞进快速层就超时。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a concrete model + latency + tier directly shows engineering judgment about budget-driven encoder tradeoffs.
'SOTA large model' without latency or tier reveals no grasp of tier budgets — empty words.
'Any works' dodges the core tradeoff, and fusion can't recover information a weak encoder lost.
Naming the largest model ignores the latency budget; a huge model in the fast tier times out.

scenario: 收尾:一句话串起内容审核模型架构的三段与关键取舍。
scenario_en: Wrap-up: one line tying together the moderation architecture's three stages and key tradeoffs.
q: 补全内容审核模型架构的骨架:
q_en: Fill in the skeleton of the content-moderation model architecture:
text: 架构三段:per-modality {{编码器}}(各模态→定长嵌入)→ {{fusion}} 融合层(快速层用 early、慢速层用 {{attention}})→ {{分层}}集成(Tier 1 <50ms 扛 85-95%,Tier 2 深判 5-15% 难件)。全程输出良好 {{校准}} 的置信度,驱动分层路由与主动学习飞轮。
text_en: Three stages: per-modality {{encoders}} (each modality to a fixed-dim embedding) → a {{fusion}} layer (early in the fast tier, {{attention}} in the slow tier) → a {{tiered}} ensemble (Tier 1 <50ms handles 85-95%, Tier 2 deep-classifies the 5-15% hard items). All emit well-{{calibrated}} confidence driving tier routing and the active-learning flywheel.
why: 一句话骨架:编码→融合→分层,置信度贯穿。快速层用便宜融合扛多数、慢速层用 attention 抓跨模态难件,校准置信度既做路由又喂飞轮。
why_en: The one-line skeleton: encode → fuse → tier, with calibrated confidence throughout driving both routing and the flywheel.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个不同成本/精度的模型分层协作:便宜层处理多数,昂贵层专攻少数难件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tiered ensemble layers models of different cost/accuracy: a cheap tier handles the majority, an expensive tier the few hard items.
